cards.body:
NVIDIA will host a conference call on Tuesday, November 17, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) to discuss its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, which ended October 25, 2026.

The call will be webcast live (in listen-only mode) on investor.nvidia.com. The company’s prepared remarks will be followed by a Q&A session, which will be limited to questions from financial analysts and institutional investors.

Ahead of the call, NVIDIA will provide written commentary on its third-quarter results from Colette Kress, the company’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. This material will be posted to investor.nvidia.com immediately after the company’s results are publicly announced at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT.

The webcast will be recorded and available for replay until the company’s conference call to discuss financial results for its fourth quarter and fiscal year 2027.

cards.body: LG전자가 올해 3분기 매출 23조8241억원, 영업이익 7819억원을 기록했다. 전년 동기 대비 매출은 8.9%, 영업이익은 13.5% 증가했다. 영업이익률은 3.3%다. 3분기 누적 매출은 71조3778억원, 영업이익은 4조347억원으로 각각 전년 동기 대비 9.2%, 55.9% 늘었다. 생활가전과 전장 사업이 안정적인 수익성을 유지한 가운데 TV 사업의 실적 개선이 두드러졌다. 미디어엔터테인먼트솔루션(MS)사업본부는 지난해 3분기 3026억원의 영업손실에서 올해 1467억원의 영업이익을 내며 흑자전환했다. 전장 사업을 담당하는 VS사업본부는 매출 2조8261억원, 영업이익 1903억원으로 역대 3분기 최대 실적을 기록했다. 신사업에서도 성과가 나타났다. 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터 냉각솔루션 누적 수주액은 3분기 기준 3조원을 넘어섰다. 상반기 6000억원 수준에서 크게 증가한 규모다. LG전자는 2200억원을 투자해 미국 생산거점 확보 등 국내외 생산능력을 확대하고 있다. 로봇 사업에서는 액추에이터 양산 준비와 글로벌 고객사 대상 수주 활동을 병행하고 있다. LG전자는 4분기에도 기업간거래(B2B)와 가전 구독 사업을 확대하고 공급망 다변화와 운영 효율화를 통해 수익성을 확보할 계획이다. 다만 중동 전쟁 장기화와 메모리·LCD 패널 등 주요 부품 가격 상승, 글로벌 소비심리 위축은 부담 요인으로 꼽힌다. 아래는 실적발표 후 컨퍼런스콜 전문이다. 참석자는 김창태 최고재무책임자(CFO) 부사장, 유종인 HS본부 경영관리담당, 박상호 MS본부 경영관리담당 전무, 김주용 VS본부 경영관리담당 상무, 신동훈 ES본부 경영관리담당 상무, 박지환 경영관리담당 전무, 김영균 금융담당 상무, 이재모 로보틱스전략담당 상무, 박인근 회계담당, 홍성민 ESG사무국장, 박원재 IR담당 상무 등이다. [2026년 3분기 경영실적 리뷰와 4분기 전망] (김창태 CFO 부사장) 2026년 3분기 연결 기준 매출은 23조8000억원, 영업이익은 7819억원을 기록했다. 전년 동기 대비 매출과 영업이익 모두 개선됐다. 중동 전쟁 악화와 주요국 금리 인상 기조 등 비우호적인 사업 환경에도 주력 사업의 시장 지위와 차별화된 경쟁력을 바탕으로 매출 성장을 이어갔다. 가전과 전장 사업에서 안정적인 수익성을 유지했고, TV 사업에서도 전년 동기 대비 큰 폭의 실적 개선을 이뤘다. 특히 전장 사업은 7개 분기 연속 한 자릿수 중반 이상의 영업이익률을 유지하며 B2B 기반의 안정적인 현금 창출원으로 자리 잡았다. 차량 무선통신 기술 혁신과 자율주행 기능 확산에 대응해 혁신 제품 개발과 사업 확대를 추진할 계획이다. 4분기에는 금리와 원자재 가격, 환율 등 다양한 경영 환경의 불확실성이 이어질 것으로 예상한다. 국가별 경제 상황에 따른 지역별 수요 편차도 심화될 전망이다. 이에 B2B 사업 확대와 글로벌 사우스 전략, 프리미엄·보급형 제품을 동시에 공략하는 투트랙 전략을 정교하게 추진해 성장 동력을 확보하겠다. 저원가 국가의 현지 제조 생태계 활용을 확대하고 글로벌 생산거점 운영의 효율성을 높일 계획이다. 공급선 다변화를 통해 대외 변수에 따른 원가구조 변동에도 유연하게 대응하겠다. [AI 데이터센터 냉각솔루션 사업 추진 현황] AI 데이터센터 냉각솔루션 사업은 수주 성과가 구체화되고 있다. 지난 2분기 컨퍼런스콜에서 상반기 수주액이 6000억원을 넘었고 연말까지 수조원 규모의 수주가 예상된다고 밝힌 바 있다. 이후 AI 데이터센터 인프라 플랫폼 기업인 에어컨트롤컨셉트(Air Control Concept)와 5기가와트(GW) 규모 AI 데이터센터에 냉각솔루션을 공급하는 계약을 체결했다. 이를 포함한 올해 3분기 누적 수주액은 3조원을 넘어섰다. 이번 계약은 단발성 프로젝트가 아니라 수년간 안정적인 매출을 확보할 수 있는 장기 공급계약이다. AI 데이터센터 냉각 시장에서 LG전자의 지위를 강화하는 계기가 될 것으로 평가한다. 빠르게 증가하는 수주 물량에 대응하기 위해 생산능력 확대 투자도 진행하고 있다. 내년 중 미국 버지니아주에 연면적 3만2000㎡, 부지면적 17만㎡ 규모의 생산거점을 신설할 예정이다. 국내 평택과 창원에도 신규 생산라인을 구축한다. 관련 투자 규모는 약 2200억원이며 향후 수주 증가에 따라 단계적으로 확대할 계획이다. 제품 포트폴리오도 확장하고 있다. 기존 칠러와 공랭식 제품에 더해 액체냉각 솔루션의 핵심 설비인 냉각수분배장치(CDU)의 기술 개발과 제품화를 추진하고 있다. 최근 엔비디아로부터 600킬로와트(kW), 1메가와트(MW), 2.6MW CDU에 대한 승인을 획득했다. 특히 2.6MW CDU는 엔비디아 AI 팩토리 플랫폼에 대응할 수 있는 제품임을 의미하는 'DSX Ready' 인증도 추가로 받았다. 이를 통해 차세대 AI 데이터센터에 대응할 수 있는 기술 역량을 입증하고 본격적인 사업 전개 기반을 확보했다. 향후 다수의 고밀도 AI 서버를 하나의 장비로 관리할 수 있는 대용량 CDU 개발을 주도하고 프로젝트 수주를 확대할 계획이다. [로보틱스 사업 추진 현황] 로보틱스 사업은 핵심 부품과 완제품 하드웨어 제조뿐 아니라 데이터 플랫폼과 운영 시스템 등 가치사슬 전반을 아우르는 솔루션 공급자로 자리 잡는 것을 목표로 하고 있다. 로봇 핵심 부품인 액추에이터는 상반기 창원에 파일럿 생산라인을 구축했다. 하반기에는 설비 자동화와 품질 경쟁력 강화 등 양산 준비 작업을 진행하고 있다. 이를 통해 로봇의 원가 및 품질 경쟁력을 높이고 시장 형성 초기 단계부터 부품 표준화 선점 등의 경쟁우위를 확보할 계획이다. 글로벌 잠재 고객을 대상으로 본격적인 수주 활동도 병행하고 있다. 휴머노이드 로봇 개발에서는 올해 4분기 서울 우면동에 국내 최대 규모의 로봇 학습 및 데이터 확보 거점인 LG 데이터팩토리를 본격 가동할 예정이다. cards.body: Nvidia and Oracle have announced general availability of Nvidia’s Vera Rubin NVL72 rack and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Superclusters at Oracle AI World on Tuesday. The announcement comes hot on the heels of Google Cloud announcing general availability for Vera Rubin last week, putting two major hyperscaler feathers in Nvidia’s cap. However, Oracle’s announcement is interesting, specifically calling out standalone Vera instances on OCI Superclusters. We've included a few benchmarks we've performed on a Vera server for a forthcoming review to highlight some of the chip's performance characteristics, but do note that these tests were not conducted on OCI infrastructure. Neoclouds have been banging the drum of Vera for the past several weeks, with instances under way at Nscale, CoreWeave, and Nebius, among others, so it makes sense to see Vera in the GPU-dominant and AI-focused neoclouds. A standalone deployment at a hyperscaler like Oracle sends a different signal, however. Although hyperscalers maintain large fleets of hardware, sometimes even renting from the neoclouds, the CPU focus is primarily on x86, with OCI Superclusters otherwise offering the Ampere Altra for an Arm-based instance. It’s Nvidia’s first standalone CPU push into the hyperscale data center, placing Vera alongside the x86 competition regardless of the GPU compute. Vera is not meant to upend the x86 guard, at least in isolation. Ian Buck, Nvidia’s mind behind CUDA and the face of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure buildout, said in March — when the chip was revealed — that the world couldn’t be served by a single, 88-core SKU. However, Vera is opening the door at hyperscalers like Oracle to expand in future CPU generations. AMD and Intel maintain the lead when it comes to single-socket density, which is only set to expand in the next generation, as AMD’s upcoming EPYC Venice CPUs can pack up to 512 threads in a single socket. However, Vera offers some distinct advantages due to its topology depending on the workload, many of which are becoming increasingly relevant in the agentic AI era. Memory bandwidth, for instance, is one of Vera’s strong suits, and that’s not just a marketing claim. Nvidia has said the memory system is capable of 1.2 TB/s of bandwidth, but we can see Nvidia’s lead outside of theoretical numbers in our testing below. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Take the industry-standard Stream benchmark as an example. We’re showing triad here, as it’s the most “demanding” of Stream’s operations, but the leads for Vera are similar across add, copy, and scale as well. cards.body: Malaysian customs have seized over $12 million (49.5 million Malaysian ringgit) worth of advanced AI chips in a single bust, as the country clamps down on a suspected semiconductor smuggling syndicate. According to a Reuters report on October 28 , officials found 30 servers containing the chips at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s free trade zone on October 15th. Initial investigations revealed that the shipment originated in an Asian country and was bound for another undisclosed Asian country. Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible The airport’s customs director, Aspalila Ag Tuah, confirmed that the servers were falsely declared as ordinary electronic goods, saying the suspected scheme used Malaysia as a transit point to avoid restrictions on the goods’ onward movement. The Malaysian company involved in the shipment has been summoned to assist in the investigation. Authorities suspect that the foiled smuggling attempt was carried out by the same group responsible for a similar attempt last June. On June 5, customs officers discovered 72 server units containing advanced AI chips at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport, valued at approximately $13 million. This shipment had also been falsely declared as computer components and was meant to be reshipped without the required permit. Aspalila said the network has been linked to seizures worth over $25 million so far across at least five cases. She declined to provide further information on the network or the current case, citing ongoing investigations. Several key facts remain unknown, including the chip type, country of manufacture, final destination, and intended recipient — whether a company or a military organization. The U.S. had placed export controls on the movement of advanced Nvidia and other U.S.-origin AI chips to China , the most likely destination for the seized chips. Smuggling networks began using Malaysia, a U.S. ally not affected by the controls, as a hub, exporting the banned chips to the country before re-exporting them to China. While the country’s geographic location and mature logistics infrastructure make it important for legitimate international trade, these characteristics also make it ideal for smuggling sensitive technology. To restrict this avenue, Malaysia subsequently imposed export controls on the ​movement of advanced AI chips of U.S. origin , at Washington’s request. Other Asian U.S. allies, such as Singapore and Taiwan, have implemented similar controls. Demand for powerful Nvidia GPUs remains high in China, fueling a booming market for smuggled hardware .

headlines.body: Google has spent years pitching customers on the advantage of buying its chips, models and cloud services in one place, offering a full stack that rivals Amazon and Microsoft have tried to replicate. Now, the company is pushing its equipment outside of its own walls to reach more customers and build a bigger business around artificial intelligence chips, a market that Nvidia has dominated. A day ahead of its third-quarter earnings report, Alphabet said Tuesday that Oracle will offer Google's tensor processing units, or TPUs, the custom chips the internet giant has been developing since 2013. It's the first time customers will be able to access TPUs outside of Google's infrastructure, and shows that cloud boss Thomas Kurian, who previously spent more than 20 years at Oracle, is looking elsewhere for growth. "They're a very strong competitor, and it's very possible that they could eventually take market share from Nvidia," said Chris Ballard, managing director of Check Capital Management, referring to Google's position in chips. Kurian, who joined Google in late 2018, is operating from a position of strength. Analysts expect Google Cloud revenue to jump about 90% from a year earlier, after growing 82% in the second quarter, with TPUs contributing to its momentum. "Google was great at doing its own thing, but it was never able to serve customers," said Uday Cheruvu, a portfolio manager at Harding Loevner, which owns Alphabet shares. "That mindset has changed." Google opened up TPUs to outside data centers in the second quarter, before this week's announcement with Oracle. Estimates for the TPU business vary widely, but they all point to significant growth. TD Cowen models $9.4 billion in TPU sales for the second half of this year and $62.5 billion for 2027. Wells Fargo expects about $9 billion in third-quarter sales and $99 billion next year. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said on the last earnings call in July that only a small portion of TPU revenue from existing agreements will be recognized this year, with the "vast majority" coming in 2027. She also said Google planned to use more outside capacity in the third quarter while the company builds out its own infrastructure. With $25 billion in second-quarter cloud revenue, Google trailed Amazon Web Services at $42 billion and Microsoft Azure at $29 billion. But Google is growing the fastest. headlines.body: Blockchain venture company Blockmate Ventures is set to enter the neocloud market, having partnered with Scannit for the purchase of eight Nvidia B200 GPUs. Under the terms of the deal, Blockmate will own the hardware, while Scannit will operate and sell the compute from an undisclosed US-based data center. Blockmate said the GPUs had a purchase price of $635,000, including shipping, data center setup, installation, network connectivity, and onboarding. The acquisition will be funded through a combination of Blockmate's existing cash resources and debt financing, with the blockchain company set to receive the majority of the gross revenue generated by the cluster. Delivery of the GPUs is slated for Q1 2027, subject to vendor timing and Nvidia allocation. Following delivery, the hardware is expected to be installed, tested, and made available to commercial customers within one week. In a statement, Blockmate said that, depending on the success of this new business model, it will evaluate future deployments, including larger clusters and future Nvidia hardware generations. "This is Blockmate's first direct step into the AI neocloud market. We will own the Nvidia hardware, while Scannit provides the specialist infrastructure, operations and customer relationships required to keep that compute working,” said Domenic Carosa, founder and chairman of Blockmate. "We are deliberately starting with one node. The objective is to get it online, generate revenue and build real operating data around utilization, pricing and costs. Based on the economics we are seeing today, we believe the initial capital invested in the node has the potential to be recovered in approximately two years, although actual results will depend on utilization, market pricing and operating costs." Founded in 2010 as Midpoint Holdings, the blockchain company rebranded to Blockmate in 2022, focusing on AI, Bitcoin, and digital infrastructure. In June 2025, Blockmate announced the launch of its dedicated Bitcoin mining business, called Blockmate Mining, with the subsidiary targeting up to 200MW of mining capacity in Wyoming as part of a long-term Bitcoin holding strategy. In a statement announcing the purchase of the B200s, Blockmate said it is continuing to advance its Wyoming AI data center development, with the 200MW of capacity, “subject to zoning, power availability, engineering, permitting, and other development requirements.”
